verdict: TIME MATTERS -- the response RESHAPES between 24h and 72h (A549, 47 drugs; the closest available time test). The 24h and 72h profiles correlate at only Spearman 0.062 (mover Jaccard 0.128): 77% of 24h movers are TRANSIENT (gone by 72h) and 77% of 72h movers are ADAPTIVE (new by 72h). A single steady-state snapshot genuinely MISSES a large amount of time-specific structure -- direct support for the transient hypothesis behind the compensation wall. NOISE CAVEAT (honest): for weakly-responding drugs the 24h/72h mover sets are near-noise, so the ~77% transient/adaptive fraction is likely INFLATED by the same per-drug pseudobulk noise seen in the saturation test; but the near-zero profile correlation even over the union of movers, plus the biology (24h=acute response, 72h=adapted survivor state for cytotoxic drugs), support a genuine large reshape for responding drugs. SECOND CAVEAT: this is 24h-vs-72h CHEMICAL perturbation (A549), NOT the 2-12h GENETIC window where paralog compensation is expected -- so it shows time-resolution matters and transient/adaptive movers are real and large, but it is a proxy, not the exact experiment. The exact test (sub-24h genetic perturb-seq) remains unavailable as a clean h5ad (would need GEO MTX assembly) and is the real highest-value next fetch.
